summary: Peter von Bradke was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tartu under Leo Meyer, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, Jena under Berthold Delbrück (Ph.D.), Munich, Leipzig, and Giessen (Habilitation). He taught at the University of Giessen from 1884 to 1896.

Peter von Köppen was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the National University of Kharkiv (~1812–1814) and the University of Tübingen (~1819–1821). Around 1837, he held a post at the Ministry of State Property.

Petr Sgall was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Charles University (~1945–1949) under doctoral supervisor Vincenc Lesný. He subsequently held an academic post at Charles University from around 1953 to 2019.

Petra Kieffer-Pülz is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Heinz Bechert. She has held posts at the University of Göttingen (attested 1995), Mainz Academy of Sciences and Literature (attested 2013, 2016), and Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

Petra Maurer is a Tibetologist and Indologist who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She has held posts at Erlangen (2017), the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013, 2026), LMU Munich (attested 2018, 2026), and Göttingen Academy (attested 2026).

id: P:Petrus Abraham Samuel van Limburg Brouwer
summary: Petrus Abraham Samuel van Limburg Brouwer was an Indologist who earned his Dr.juris at the University of Groningen (1844–1850). In 1865, he held a research post at the Nationaal Archief.

Phakchok Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Dzongsar Institute (Khenpo title) and trained under traditional teachers including Nyoshul Khenpo, Dilgo Khyentse, and Tulku Urgyen. He serves as Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling.

Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where she studied under MA supervisors Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

Phanit Jetjiravat studied Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, completing a Master of Arts under academic advisors Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn was a Sinologist and historian who studied at Harvard, SOAS, the Defense Language Institute, and Georgetown. He held faculty posts at the University of Chicago (1963–1978), Harvard University (from 1978), and directed the Fairbank Center (1980–1986).

Philip A. Mellor is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester by 1989. He served as Professor of Religion and Social Theory at the University of Leeds (attested 2010).
Philip Anderson was an Indologist and historian who earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge (~1834–1838). He later served as Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1855–1857).

Philip Boas Yampolsky worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University (Ph.D. 1965) and under Yoshitaka Iriya. He served as Columbia's East Asian Library librarian and professor (1968–1996) and chaired the Numata Center (1991–1996).

Philip C. Almond is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Adelaide (1975–1980). In 1982, he became an emeritus professor at the University of Queensland.

Philip Clart is a Sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Daniel L. Overmyer (~1992–1997). In ~2008, he was appointed Professor of Chinese Culture and History at the University of Leipzig.

Philip Deslippe is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Connecticut (BA), University of Iowa (MA), and University of California, Santa Barbara, where he was attested as a teaching associate in 2020.

Philip Kapleau was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Soen Nakagawa, Sogaku Harada, and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani. He founded the Rochester Zen Center and the Chapin Mill Retreat Center (1996).

Philip L. Quinn was a philosopher who studied at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He taught at Brown University (~1970–1985), was named O'Brien Professor at Notre Dame in 1985, and served as President of the American Philosophical Association (1994–1995).

Philip Lutgendorf is an Indologist who earned his B.A. at the University of Chicago (~1967–1987). He joined the University of Iowa faculty in 1985 and served as President of the American Institute of Indian Studies (2010–2018).

Philip Novak is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Notre Dame and Syracuse University. Around 1980, he held a teaching post at Dominican University of California.
